### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b8bce40e081477132d81b1e11a19cd3cdb331c0`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/data/:object (route, 68 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b8bce40e081477132d81b1e11a19cd3cdb331c0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1cfb55844dc259cd25ab358cd474e0e8df60a3e8` — the merge of head `90e4e4d69e9f1bf7fc42ee7336528d9ece161e73` into base `0b8bce40e081477132d81b1e11a19cd3cdb331c0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1cfb55844dc259cd25ab358cd474e0e8df60a3e8 && git checkout 1cfb55844dc259cd25ab358cd474e0e8df60a3e8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0b8bce40e081477132d81b1e11a19cd3cdb331c0 90e4e4d69e9f1bf7fc42ee7336528d9ece161e73 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0b8bce40e081477132d81b1e11a19cd3cdb331c0 && git merge --no-ff 90e4e4d69e9f1bf7fc42ee7336528d9ece161e73

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b8bce40e081477132d81b1e11a19cd3cdb331c0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0b8bce40e081477132d81b1e11a19cd3cdb331c0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.page-window.test.ts, packages/rest/src/data-page-window-door.test.ts + packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server-query-number-census.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts; prose face read for ②: .changeset/25229-page-window-refused.md

Inputs: card #25229 (body; both comments: claim 6344422865, dev report 6346424315), PR #25260 body with Acceptance notes, file list (4 files, +407/−2) and net diff against merge base `345f0b154c`, and the check-runs on the head, read 2026-10-22T17:09Z: 27 success, 7 skipped, 6 in_progress — the six `Test Core` shards; `Check Changeset` success with its ADR-0087 step success; `Dogfood Regression Gate` success; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Choke point — RIGHT for the three doors the PR names, verified by trace.** `GET /data/:object` hands `req.query` whole to `findData` (`crud-routes.ts`). `POST /data/:object/query` parses `FindDataRequestSchema` for validation only and forwards the ORIGINAL body; the spec's transport lowering (`lowerFoldedTransportValues`, `data-engine.zod.ts`) refuses a non-numeric string and converts a numeric one but checks neither sign nor integrality, so `offset: -5` and `limit: 1.5` pass the schema and meet `pageWindowValue` — one check, no second validator on one door. The runtime dispatcher's GET list and POST query (`domains/data.ts`) reach the same statement through `callData('query')` → `protocol.findData`; its envelope (`resolveThrownHttpError`) reads `.status` before `.statusCode` and keeps a `.code` the closed `ErrorCode` vocabulary knows, so that door answers 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` too (by reading — no pin in this PR; the same path the repeated-parameter refusal already takes). Internal callers pass literal or schema-read integers and are unaffected: import-runner (`limit: 2`, `ids.length` ≥ 1), connector-pull (`limit: 1`), import-job load (`limit: 1`), import-jobs list (`readDeclaredQueryNumber` against `int()` schemas, blank = absent). The SDK (`packages/client`) sends `limit`/`offset` as numbers over POST and never spells a blank `$top=`. A direct `engine.find` caller bypasses the statement — not a Data API door, correctly left out. A flow or action `query` whose authored window is fractional or negative (`action-execution.ts`) is now refused instead of silently paged: a narrowing inside the card's rule, named here.

**(a) — WRONG: one server-built caller feeds a derived FLOAT into the statement.** The export door `GET /data/:object/export` computes `chunkSize = Math.min(5000, Math.max(50, Number(q.page) || 500))` with no floor (`data-action-routes.ts`, the `chunkSize` line), so `?page=100.5` — any fractional `page` inside the 50–5000 clamp — makes `take = 100.5`, and the loop's first `findData` now throws 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` naming `limit`, a parameter the caller never wrote (the #4226 discipline this card cites), on a door the changeset does not name, where the base streamed the full export (knex truncates; the PR's own base row `limit: 1.5` → 200, 1 row shows it). That door's #20139 ledgered exemption states in code that `page` sets only the chunk size and that refusing one "would turn a correct export into a 400"; its census pin (`rest-server-query-number-census.test.ts`, the `page` enumeration) lists `'1.5'`, `'Infinity'`, `'-5'`, `'50'`, `'5000'` — every one of which clamps to an integer — and drives a STUB `findData`, so the pin stays green through exactly this regression and CI cannot see it. Remedy in the same PR: integerise the chunk at its source (`Math.trunc` on the read `page`, keeping the 50/5000 clamp) and add a `page` value that lands fractional after clamping (`'100.5'`) to the census pin, asserting every `limit` the loop hands `findData` is a safe integer; the export door's accept set is then unchanged and the changeset's door list stands. (The claim's own condition for touching the REST door — the shared normalizer cannot see the caller's spelling — is met here.)

**(b) Refusal — RIGHT.** `pageWindowValue` reads only the two arms a door can deliver (number, non-blank string) and accepts a non-negative safe integer; the spelling comes from `slotParam(canonical)` = `wireSpelling` ∘ `arrivedAs`, so each of `$top`/`top`/`limit`/`$skip`/`skip`/`offset` is quoted as written — pinned ×17 in the unit file with `code`, `status`, `param`, the first clause, and `engine.find` never called. `INVALID_REQUEST` is registered in the ledger for `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/rest`; no ledger move. 400 reaches the wire through `mapDataError` → `classifyDataError` (declared-status passthrough); the door file pins status, `code` and message over a real `RestServer` handler and a real `SqlDriver` with zero reads of the object. `limit: 0`, `$top=0`, `$skip=0` accepted and pinned on both doors. Accept-set edges worth knowing, none a narrowing: a string goes through `Number()` after the blank check, so `'0x10'`, `'1e2'`, `'+5'`, `' 5 '` are accepted exactly as before (the changeset's "non-negative integers" slightly overstates the grammar); `true` is now refused where `Number(true)` was `1` (reachable only from in-process callers — the POST schema already refused booleans); `Infinity` and values above `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are refused, right for a driver bound. The runtime string carries no tracker number.

**(c) Blanks — RIGHT.** The card allows "400, or treated as absent"; refusing both `$top=` and `$skip=` is the consistent choice, and it is the spec's own stance already — `lowerFoldedTransportValues` reads a blank string as NaN and refuses it on the POST door — so reading a blank `$skip` as absent on GET would leave the two doors disagreeing on one input. `$skip=` was not in the card's table; its refusal is a narrowing beyond the rows, inside the card's rule, and declared in the changeset.

**(d) POST body schema — RIGHT, with a follow-up, not a FAIL.** No second validator exists on one door, and the documented-vs-enforced split stands: `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.limit`/`offset` are `z.number()` and the transport `$top`/`$skip` are number-or-string, so the published schema advertises negatives and fractions the server now refuses with a 400 (before, a 500 or a silently truncated page — declared ≠ enforced pre-existed in a quieter form). Follow-up card for the spec lane (cross-lane, declared on #18549 per the claim): declare `.int().nonnegative()` on `limit`/`offset` and the transport spellings so declared = enforced, with its own `Clause-②` and `Metadata-protocol` reading.

### ② Semver level

RIGHT. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is line-initial in the PR body and the changeset; `Metadata-protocol: none` (a request window is not authored metadata) ⇒ `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (published, `18.0.0`) per AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3; the BREAKING banner is present (`!` in the title, the bold banner in the body); exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, read against the detector — no arrow rewrite, no FROM/TO label, no framed heading, no rewrite table — so the category holds, and the head's `Check Changeset` job ran "Require an ADR-0087 disposition on a declared-breaking changeset" to success; `patch` clears the no-major guard. `packages/rest` receives a test file only, so no changeset is owed there. The `(narrowing)` arm's dogfood is pinned to the head in the dev report (`8845dd244`, VERDICT command-exit 0, 287 files passed and 3 skipped, 2398 tests passed and 18 skipped) and `Dogfood Regression Gate` is success on the head. The changeset's door list is correct only with the ①(a) remedy applied; without it the export door narrows undeclared.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` (blank `$skip=`): answered — keep it refused, for the reason in ①(c).
- Acceptance note 1 (the message's second sentence omits the truncated fractional case): acceptable — the first clause is the pinned contract and the sentence names the two loud failure classes; tighten the prose if the patch round touches the function, not required.
- Acceptance note 2 (a direct `engine.find` with `offset: -1` still meets knex's throw): out of the card's scope by the claim; an in-process caller's mistake answered by a thrown Error is loud, not silent — no card owed. `out_of_scope_findings` carries it with no carrier, consistent.
- Deviations: the branch is the platform-designated `claude/project-thread-6i4obw` (the claim records it; "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" is success); the attribution link; the test-only file in `packages/rest`; not re-merged with `origin/main` (the queue rebuilds on current `main`) — all acceptable.
- Not measured here: the shipped console's querystring spelling (`packages/console/dist` is absent in this checkout); the SDK spells numbers over POST.
- Check-runs: the six `Test Core` shards were still in_progress at the reading above, so the new tests' CI verdict is not yet in; the lane seat reads them to success before any queueing, as always.
